subject: Request: Graduated-Commit Early Release & Downsell Credit — Exec Approval
messages:
From: Kendra Alvarez <kendra@stratahealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Strata Health Procurement <procure@stratahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Early exit / flexible downsell for pilot commitment

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed by the latency and cost profile on the Redwood Dedicated runs. We're moving fast internally, but procurement and finance are pushing back on the full 12-month commitment in the SOW.

We need two things to move forward quickly:
- A mechanism to exit early into a smaller committed tier (a "graduated-commit" path) with a clear schedule of credits/fees if we downscale in months 1–6 vs 7–12.
- An opt-out / release clause that allows us to reduce committed spend with 60 days' notice after month 6 if product metrics don't align with our needs.

Can you share what flexibility is possible on credits and contract language? Procurement also asked for a draft payment schedule.

Kendra
Director of Engineering, StrataHealth

--
Sent from my phone
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Kendra Alvarez <kendra@stratahealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Early exit / flexible downsell for pilot commitment

Kendra — appreciate the transparency. We're aligned on wanting Strata to get value quickly and for you to feel comfortable with the commitment.

Summary of what we can propose immediately (high level):
- Graduated-commit schedule: if Strata reduces committed GPU capacity in months 1–3, we can offer a 40% downsell credit on remaining committed value; months 4–6 a 25% credit; months 7–12 a 10% credit (applies to committed baseline only).
- Opt-out language: a one-time opt-out after month 6 with 60 days' notice; opt-out results in downsell credit per schedule above and a final reconciliation invoice.
- Conditions: credits apply only if there are no outstanding invoices and if usage is within expected ranges; credits are one-time and not refundable cash (applied to future bills or final reconciliation).

I've attached a proposed SOW and a payment schedule (first pass) for procurement to review.

Because the proposed credits exceed our standard delegation (sales ops cap is 25%), I need an exec sign-off to proceed. Priyom can summarize the commercial rationale below.

Attachments: SOW_StrataHealth_Q4_2026.pdf, payment_schedule_strata_v2.xlsx

Marcus
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Deal Desk <deals@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Early exit / flexible downsell for pilot commitment — request for approval

Forwarding for formal review and approval. TL;DR: StrataHealth wants a graduated-commit early-release path with significant downsell credits that exceed our sales delegation. Key facts:
- ACV: $480k (12-month committed GPU + dedicated support).
- Proposed max downsell credit: 40% in months 1–3, stepping down after month 3.
- Strategic considerations: Strata is a high-visibility customer in digital health; referenceability and likelihood to expand into other lines (analytics, embeddings) is high if pilot succeeds.
- Risk: If we allow large credits without guardrails we create a precedent for future enterprise deals.

Ask: Exec approval to grant a capped, one-time downsell credit schedule as Marcus proposed, with the following guardrails:
1) Credits applied to invoices only; no cash refunds.
2) SOW addendum capturing opt-out after month 6 with 60 days' notice.
3) CS must complete a health check at month 3 that confirms adoption signals; if negative, expedited partner engagement is required.
4) Credit cap: maximum total credit exposure of $150k (not to exceed 31% of ACV).

I've attached negotiation notes and the SOW Marcus shared. Please advise approval/changes.

Priyom
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Early exit / flexible downsell for pilot commitment — request for approval

Thanks for the context. I approve the proposed graduated-commit early-release path with the following explicit conditions (must be reflected in the SOW/addendum before signature):
1) Credit schedule as proposed (40% months 1–3; 25% months 4–6; 10% months 7–12) but total credit exposure capped at $150,000.
2) Credits are non-refundable and will be applied as account-level credit against future invoices or final reconciliation.
3) Opt-out allowed only once and only after month 6 with 60 days' notice; opt-out triggers reconciliation as described.
4) Customer must sign a one-page addendum acknowledging the credit mechanics and that credits cannot be used for prior unpaid invoices.
5) CS and Solutions must co-sign the SOW (Marcus to loop in CS for month-3 health check and measurable success criteria).
6) Legal (Laura) to confirm the addendum language; no other non-standard indemnity or data terms approved here.

If Laura signs off on the addendum language and Solutions confirms success criteria, Marcus — please proceed to issue the updated SOW and DocuSign link to Kendra.

Aditya
Chief Revenue Officer, Redwood Inference
